conventions.pose: 4x4 camera/local-to-world homogeneous matrix; row-major nested arrays
conventions.preview: Deterministic synthetic trace playback; intermediate graphics are visual interpolation.

notes: Synthetic measurements: Gaussian 0.35 px coordinate noise plus 12 labeled outlier observations.
Two anchor cameras are fixed at ground truth, including a fixed metric baseline; the other four optimize all six pose degrees of freedom.
Every state is an accepted LM iterate. Its Huber IRLS linearization is recomputed at that same state.
Block norms use Frobenius norm. Camera block matrix includes two zero anchor rows/columns; cross blocks and Schur use only four free cameras.
Schur matrix includes diagonal-scaled LM damping at the displayed lambda. RMSE is Euclidean image distance per observation.
Fourteen deterministic, diverse, noise-free synthetic motion pairs satisfy A X = X B.
Residual is Log((A X)^-1 X B), whitened by 0.30 m translation and 0.35 rad rotation scales.
Actual six-DOF left-increment LM optimization uses central finite-difference Lie residual Jacobians and per-pair Huber reweighting.
A is a robot-frame relative motion and B is the matching camera-frame relative motion; X maps camera coordinates into robot coordinates.
motionPath starts at identity and accumulates robot motions on the right: G_next = G A. Camera-to-world poses are G X, so their relative motions equal B.
X is one constant unknown camera-to-robot calibration; all displayed matrices use the same explicit convention.
Static noncoplanar six-point target, pinhole camera, known true current point depths, no measurement noise.
Image-based control v = -gain (L^T L + damping^2 I)^-1 L^T e uses normalized image coordinates.
Camera-to-world poses integrate camera-frame body velocity with T_next = T Exp(dt v).
Every recorded state is one actual simulation step; visual interpolation does not create solver steps.
